records.explanation: Variant B converts at 44.4% against 39.7% for A, a two-proportion z-score of 7.43, well above the 1.96 threshold for 95% significance.
records.sql:
WITH e AS (
  SELECT experiment_id
  FROM reporting.experiments
  WHERE experiment_name = 'Product page: new screenshots'
),
v AS (
  SELECT variant,
         SUM(taps)::float8 AS n,
         SUM(installs)::float8 AS x
  FROM reporting.experiment_daily
  WHERE experiment_id IN (SELECT experiment_id FROM e)
    AND variant IN ('A', 'B')
  GROUP BY variant
),
w AS (
  SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'A' THEN n END) AS na,
         MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'A' THEN x END) AS xa,
         MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'B' THEN n END) AS nb,
         MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'B' THEN x END) AS xb
  FROM v
),
s AS (
  SELECT na, xa, nb, xb,
         xa / na AS cr_a,
         xb / nb AS cr_b,
         (xa + xb) / (na + nb) AS p_pooled
  FROM w
)
SELECT cr_a,
       cr_b,
       (cr_b - cr_a) / sqrt(p_pooled * (1 - p_pooled) * (1 / na + 1 / nb)) AS z_score,
       ABS((cr_b - cr_a) / sqrt(p_pooled * (1 - p_pooled) * (1 / na + 1 / nb))) > 1.96 AS significant_at_95
FROM s;

records.explanation: The 95% confidence interval for B's conversion rate minus A's in the 'Product page: shorter subtitle' test starts at -1.69 percentage points, so the true difference could be as low as that.
records.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT d.variant, SUM(d.taps) AS taps, SUM(d.installs) AS installs
  FROM reporting.experiment_daily d
  JOIN reporting.experiments e ON e.experiment_id = d.experiment_id
  WHERE e.experiment_name = 'Product page: shorter subtitle'
  GROUP BY d.variant
),
rates AS (
  SELECT variant, taps, installs, installs::numeric / taps AS cr
  FROM counts
)
SELECT
  ROUND(((b.cr - a.cr) - 1.96 * SQRT(a.cr * (1 - a.cr) / a.taps + b.cr * (1 - b.cr) / b.taps)) * 100, 3) AS ci_lower_pp
FROM rates a
JOIN rates b ON a.variant = 'A' AND b.variant = 'B';

records.explanation: Variant B's install rate (42.4%) is slightly below variant A's (42.6%), with a z-score of -0.31, well short of the 1.96 needed for 95% significance, so the difference could easily be chance.
records.sql:
WITH exp AS (
  SELECT experiment_id
  FROM reporting.experiments
  WHERE experiment_name = 'Product page: shorter subtitle'
),
v AS (
  SELECT d.variant,
         SUM(d.taps)::numeric AS taps,
         SUM(d.installs)::numeric AS installs
  FROM reporting.experiment_daily d
  JOIN exp USING (experiment_id)
  WHERE d.variant IN ('A', 'B')
  GROUP BY d.variant
),
w AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'A' THEN installs / NULLIF(taps, 0) END) AS cr_a,
    MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'B' THEN installs / NULLIF(taps, 0) END) AS cr_b,
    MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'A' THEN taps END) AS n_a,
    MAX(CASE WHEN variant = 'B' THEN taps END) AS n_b,
    SUM(installs) / NULLIF(SUM(taps), 0) AS pooled_cr
  FROM v
)
SELECT cr_a,
       cr_b,
       n_a,
       n_b,
       z,
       CASE WHEN ABS(z) > 1.96 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS significant_95
FROM (
  SELECT w.*,
         (cr_b - cr_a) / SQRT(pooled_cr * (1 - pooled_cr) * (1 / n_a + 1 / n_b)) AS z
  FROM w
) t;

records.explanation: "ledgerly budget" had the lowest cost per install in US dollars among keywords with at least 1,000 installs, at about $0.54 per install (1,657 installs, $896 spend).
records.sql:
WITH kw AS (
  SELECT k.keyword_id, k.keyword, c.currency
  FROM reporting.keywords k
  JOIN reporting.ad_groups ag ON ag.ad_group_id = k.ad_group_id
  JOIN reporting.campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = ag.campaign_id
),
daily AS (
  SELECT d.keyword_id, kw.keyword, d.installs,
         CASE WHEN kw.currency = 'USD' THEN d.spend
              ELSE d.spend / fx.units_per_usd
         END AS spend_usd
  FROM reporting.keyword_daily d
  JOIN kw ON kw.keyword_id = d.keyword_id
  JOIN reporting.fx_rates fx ON fx.day = d.day AND fx.currency = kw.currency
)
SELECT keyword_id,
       keyword,
       SUM(installs) AS installs,
       SUM(spend_usd) AS spend_usd,
       SUM(spend_usd) / SUM(installs) AS cost_per_install_usd
FROM daily
GROUP BY keyword_id, keyword
HAVING SUM(installs) >= 1000
ORDER BY cost_per_install_usd ASC
LIMIT 1;

  JOIN reporting.campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = ag.campaign_id
),
daily AS (
  SELECT d.keyword_id, kw.keyword, d.installs,
         CASE WHEN kw.currency = 'USD' THEN d.spend
              ELSE d.spend / fx.units_per_usd
         END AS spend_usd
  FROM reporting.keyword_daily d
  JOIN kw ON kw.keyword_id = d.keyword_id
  JOIN reporting.fx_rates fx ON fx.day = d.day AND fx.currency = kw.currency
)
SELECT keyword_id,
       keyword,
       SUM(installs) AS installs,
       SUM(spend_usd) AS spend_usd,
       SUM(spend_usd) / SUM(installs) AS cost_per_install_usd
FROM daily
GROUP BY keyword_id, keyword
HAVING SUM(installs) >= 1000
ORDER BY cost_per_install_usd ASC
LIMIT 1;
